inferno._comment: Fire as the world's condition rather than an event in it, so `molten` carries the whole of what it is and `hostile` is what that comes to for anybody standing in it. `dry` because the Age it wants is one the rain has left -- which is a fact about the phenomenon and not the weather it happens to arrive with.

aurora._comment: Bright and colourful, and no more: a tag names what a thing essentially is. This is what puts a curtain within reach of `beautiful` -- which queries colourful 1.0 and bright 0.6 -- and out of reach of `foreboding`, whose negative terms strike it out rather than dimming it. `frozen` because an aurora belongs where the snow does, which is a fact about it and not a mood.

rainbow._comment: Colour is the whole of it, and the light behind the colour is the rest. `watery` because a bow is sunlight bent through falling rain and cannot happen in a dry Age -- weakly, since the water is what it is made of rather than what it is.

sandfall._comment: A column of loose ground walking the Age, so `sandy` is what it is made of and what it leaves behind. `hostile` for the burial, and `dry` for the same reason an inferno is: the Age it belongs in is one nothing has watered.

meteors._comment: Burning rock arriving from outside the world, so `molten` is what it is made of and what it leaves in the crater, and `hostile` is the highest here -- a sandfall buries you slowly and this goes off on you. `bright` because a shower is genuinely a thing worth watching, which is what keeps it within reach of `beautiful` as well as of `savage`.

blizzard._comment: Snow driven sideways, so `frozen` is what it is made of and what it leaves. `hostile` for the burial and the freezing -- a shade above the sandfall's, since a drift takes your footing and the cold takes you. `watery` weakly, because a blizzard is precipitation however hard it has set: it needs a sky that gives something, which is the fact a bow shares and an inferno's `dry` is the inverse of.

deluge._comment: The sea coming up under rain that will not stop, so `watery` is the whole of what it is made of and what it leaves -- the only phenomenon in the set to carry it at one. `hostile` a shade under the blizzard's: a deluge takes the ground rather than taking you, and a writer who builds up is simply not in danger from it. `dark` because a drowned Age is one whose caves and low ground have gone under, and `eroded` for what a risen sea leaves of a coastline.
